prompt: Count how many cereal boxes are on each store shelf and where the gaps are.
why: Locating and counting items is object detection.
trap: A caption wouldn't give positions or counts.

prompt: Draw a box around every worker in a camera feed who isn't wearing a hard hat.
tells: Draw a box around every worker
why: Bounding boxes around objects are object detection.
trap: Tags would say 'person' but not where.

prompt: Find which parking spaces in an overhead camera image have cars in them.
why: Where objects are in the image is object detection.
trap: A description of the lot wouldn't map cars to spaces.

prompt: A model already says 'this X-ray contains a fracture'. Doctors now want to know where in the image it is.
tells: where in the image it is
why: Moving from 'what' to 'where' is classification to object detection.
trap: Knowing what's there is image classification; locating it is detection.

prompt: Count each deer in trail-camera images and mark where each one is.
why: Locating and counting is object detection.
trap: A caption might say 'deer' but not how many or where.

prompt: A quality camera must outline each scratch on a car door so a robot can polish it.
why: The robot needs locations, so it's object detection.
trap: Knowing there is a scratch isn't enough; it needs to know where.
